Got my first swim of the year in today! My normal swimming hole had too high of a bacterial count, so I tried Fox Brook Park which I hadn’t visited before. I bought a pass to Waukesha County Parks for the year to get plenty of swimming in, so figured I should tour all the parks. I’ll report back on the rest of the swimming spots as I visit them. 🏊‍♀️ This park gets a 4/5. There was plenty of parking and despite it being a 90+ F degree day there was room to set my towel down without being on top of other people. They have bathrooms, a concession stand, picnic areas and kayak rental. Trains pass by one side of the lake roughly every hour, which I enjoyed hearing, though others might not. I don’t have enough train noises in my life anymore. It gets docked a point cause the water is really warm before you hit the drop off point, but if you’re a good swimmer you can go beyond the drop off point at your own risk where the water was more refreshing, though not too cold. I was warned by a couple of kids that if you swim too far past the drop off point you might get bitten by fish, though all one of them got when they were bitten was a bruise. 😅 🏊 🏊‍♀️

Swimmers face fecal contamination at beaches along US coastline By PATRICK WHITTLE and MINGSON LAU Updated 10:15 AM EDT, August 30, 2025 OGUNQUIT, Maine (AP) — "Thousands of Americans will head to beaches for one last summer splash this Labor Day weekend, but taking a dip might be out of the question: Many of the beaches will caution against swimming because of unsafe levels of fecal contamination. "Beaches from , to , have been under advisories warning about water quality this week because of elevated levels of bacteria associated with fecal waste. The advisories typically discourage beachgoers from going in the water because the bacteria can cause gastrointestinal illness, rashes and nausea. "There have been closures this week at some of the country’s most popular beach destinations, including Keyes Memorial Beach in the village of Hyannis in Barnstable, Massachusetts; Benjamin’s Beach on in Bay Shore, New York; and a portion of the Imperial Beach shoreline near . Even on the pristine, white sand beaches of Hawaii, the Hawaii State Department of Health is warning of a high bacteria count at on the . "It’s a longstanding and widespread problem. Nearly two-thirds of beaches tested nationwide in 2024 experienced at least one day in which indicators of fecal contamination reached potentially unsafe levels, conservation group Environment America said in a report issued this summer. "The group reviewed beaches on the coasts and and found that 84% of beaches exceeded the standard at least once. The number was 79% for beaches, 54% for beaches and 71% for beaches. "The report also said more than 450 beaches were potentially unsafe for swimming on at least 25 percent of the days tested. A key reason is outdated water and that allows contamination from to reach the places where people swim, said John Rumpler, clean water director and senior attorney with . " 'These beaches are a treasure for families across New England and across the country. They are a shared resource,' said Rumpler, who is based in Boston. 'We need to make the investment to make sure that literally our own doesn’t wind up in the places where we are swimming.' "Other factors have also played a role in contaminating beaches, including increasingly that overwhelms sewage systems, and suburban sprawl that paves over natural areas and reduces the ’s ability to absorb , Rumpler said."
Failed jokes aside, the water is warm and more folks need to be in the water instead of by the beach.
